key_results.claim: GPT-2 small IOI circuit contains 26 attention heads in 7 main classes.
key_results.quote: We discover a circuit of 26 attention heads–1.1% of the total number of (head, token position) pairs–that completes the bulk of this task. The circuit uses 7 categories of heads (see Figure 2) to implement the algorithm.

key_results.claim: GPT-2 small has mean logit difference 3.56 and predicts IO over S 99.3% of the time; mean IO probability 49%.
key_results.quote: Over 100,000 dataset examples, GPT-2 small has mean logit difference of 3.56 (IO predicted over S 99.3% of the time), and mean IO probability of 49%.

key_results.claim: Full circuit achieves 87% of model performance; |F(M)-F(C)|=0.46, 13% of F(M)=3.56.
key_results.quote: For the circuit C from Figure 2, we find that |F (M ) − F (C)| = 0.46, or only 13% of F (M ) = 3.56.

key_results.claim: Knocking out all Name Mover Heads at once leaves circuit working with only 5% drop in logit difference.
key_results.quote: To our surprise, the circuit still worked (only 5% drop in logit difference).

key_results.claim: All three Name Mover Heads have copy score above 95%, compared to less than 20% for an average head.
key_results.quote: All three Name Mover Heads have a copy score above 95%, compared to less than 20% for an average head.

key_results.claim: Greedy search found incomplete sets with score up to 3.09, 87% of original logit difference.
key_results.quote: However, the third resulted in sets K that had high incompleteness score: up to 3.09 (87% of the original logit difference).

key_results.claim: Duplicating both S and IO reduces logit difference and causes model to predict S over IO 23% of the time.
key_results.quote: We find that this significantly reduces the logit difference and causes the model to predict S over IO 23% of the time (Figure 8).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Several components remain not understood, including S-Inhibition attention patterns and MLP/layer-norm effects.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we do not understand several components. Those include the attention patterns of the S-Inhibition Heads, and the effect of MLPs and layer norms.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: GPT-2 small is far smaller than state-of-the-art transformer language models.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: the number of parameters in GPT-2 small is orders of magnitude away from state-of-the-art transformer language models.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Mechanisms in adversarial examples are not fully understood.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we do not have a full understanding of the mechanisms at play in these adversarial examples.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Additional validation checks were omitted due to time constraints.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we would want to perform additional checks that we omitted due to time constraints.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Experiments do not intervene on MLPs, layer norms, or embedding matrices.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: In all of our experiments, we do not intervene on MLPs, layer norms, or embedding matrices

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper studies GPT-2 small and IOI only; it does not test whether the circuit structure transfers to Gemma 4 E2B or to KV-shared layers 15-34.
The analysis largely ignores MLPs, layer norms, and embeddings, so it may miss computation relevant to per-layer embeddings and factual recall.
Mean ablation on pABC may introduce distribution shift and can alter the causal role of components compared with natural IOI inputs.
Completeness is searched only via sampling and greedy optimization, so redundant or backup circuits may remain undiscovered.
Path patching assumes localized causal paths and may not capture nonlinear or distributed interactions across layers.
The paper does not evaluate CPU-only interpretability workflows or the scalability of these methods to larger models.
data.relevance_to_lab: Provides a template for circuit discovery with path patching, activation patching, attention-pattern analysis, and validation criteria. Its induction-head and name-mover analyses are relevant to induction-head and factual-recall tracing, but it studies GPT-2 small rather than Gemma 4 E2B KV-shared layers 15-34 or per-layer embeddings.

data.title: Interpretability in the Wild: A Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 Small
data.research_question: How does GPT-2 small implement indirect object identification (IOI), which attention-head circuit is responsible, and does that circuit satisfy faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria?

models_and_data.item: GPT-2 small, the primary model studied.
models_and_data.quote: GPT-2 small is a decoder-only transformer with 12 layers and 12 attention heads per attention layer.

models_and_data.item: The pIOI dataset, generated from IOI templates with random single-token entities.
models_and_data.quote: We create dataset samples for IOI using 15 templates (see Appendix E) with random single-token names, places and items.

models_and_data.item: The pABC distribution used as the reference distribution for mean-ablation knockouts.
models_and_data.quote: It relies on the same generation procedure, but instead of using two names (IO and S) it used three unrelated random names (A, B and C).

models_and_data.item: Entity vocabularies used to construct pIOI samples.
models_and_data.quote: Each name was drawn from a list of 100 English first names, while the place and the object were chosen among a hand-made list of 20 common words.

models_and_data.item: Random-token sequences used to validate induction behavior and duplicate detection.
models_and_data.quote: We run GPT-2 small on sequences of 100 tokens sampled uniformly at random from GPT-2’s token vocabulary.

models_and_data.item: Open Web Text, used for additional fuzzy Duplicate Token Head analysis.
models_and_data.quote: On Open Web Text (OWT), the fuzzy Duplicate Token Head attend to duplicates in a short range (see Appendix I).

models_and_data.item: GPT-2 medium, used only in a preliminary scaling analysis.
models_and_data.quote: As a starting point, we performed a preliminary analysis of GPT-2 medium.

protocol.step: Generate IOI samples from templates containing an initial clause and a main clause, with the final token required to be the indirect object.
protocol.quote: We create dataset samples for IOI using 15 templates (see Appendix E) with random single-token names, places and items.

protocol.step: Implement circuit ablations through mean ablation rather than zero ablation, using template-conditioned reference averages.
protocol.quote: To address this, we instead knockout nodes through mean ablation: replacing them with their average activation value across some reference distribution, similar to the bias correction method used in Nanda & Lieberum (2022).

protocol.step: Use path patching to substitute activations from a counterfactual input while preserving or recomputing selected paths.
protocol.quote: Path patching replaces part of a model’s forward pass with activations from a different input.

protocol.step: Trace information backward from the logits by patching each candidate head's direct path to the logit residual state and measuring the change in logit difference.
protocol.quote: To trace information back from the logits, we run path patching for the pathway h → Logits for each head h at the END position and display the effect on logit difference in Figure 3a.

protocol.step: Characterize candidate heads using attention patterns, output-direction projections, and copy-score experiments.
protocol.quote: To verify our hypothesis, we design experiments to test the heads’ functionality.

protocol.step: Disentangle token and positional signals by activation patching groups of heads with counterfactual outputs and recomputing the forward pass.
protocol.quote: In this section, we conducted activation patching (or simply patching). Instead of patching isolated paths, we patch the output of a set of heads and recompute the forward pass of the model after this modification.

protocol.step: Validate circuit quality with faithfulness, completeness, and minimality tests using uniform random knockout subsets, whole-class knockouts, and greedily optimized knockout subsets.
protocol.quote: we use three sampling methods to seek sets K that give large incompleteness scores:

protocol.step: Construct adversarial passages in which both the subject and indirect object are duplicated.
protocol.quote: Motivated by this, we constructed passages where both the S and IO tokens are duplicated.

metrics.name: Logit difference
metrics.definition: The difference between the logits of the indirect-object and subject name tokens; positive values favor the correct indirect object.
metrics.quote: Logit difference measures the difference in logit value between the two names, where a positive score means the correct name (IO) has higher probability.

metrics.name: IO probability
metrics.definition: The model's absolute probability assigned to the indirect-object token, averaged over pIOI.
metrics.quote: IO probability measures the absolute probability of the IO token under the model’s predictions.

metrics.name: Copy score
metrics.definition: The proportion of samples for which the input name token appears among the top 5 logits after simulating a head's OV write.
metrics.quote: We compute the proportion of samples that contain the input name token in the top 5 logits (N = 1000) and call this the copy score.

metrics.name: Average circuit logit difference F(C)
metrics.definition: The expected IOI logit difference produced by a circuit after all nodes outside the circuit are knocked out.
metrics.quote: We define the average logit difference F (C) = EX∼pIOI [f (C(X); X)] as a measure of how well C performs the IOI task.

metrics.name: Faithfulness
metrics.definition: The absolute performance gap between the circuit and the full model.
metrics.quote: The first one, faithfulness, asks that C has similar performance to the full model M , as measured by |F (M ) − F (C)|.

metrics.name: Completeness
metrics.definition: The requirement that the circuit and full model remain similar under every knockout subset, measured by the incompleteness score.
metrics.quote: To solve this problem, we introduce the completeness criterion: for every subset K ⊆ C, the incompleteness score |F (C \ K) − F (M \ K)| should be small.

metrics.name: Minimality
metrics.definition: The requirement that each circuit node has a recoverable effect when other nodes are knocked out.
metrics.quote: Formally, the minimality criterion is whether for every node v ∈ C there exists a subset K ⊆ C \ {v} that has high minimality score |F (C \ (K ∪ {v})) − F (C \ K)|.

key_results.claim: The identified IOI circuit contains 26 attention heads and covers a small fraction of all head-token pairs.
key_results.quote: We discover a circuit of 26 attention heads–1.1% of the total number of (head, token position) pairs–that completes the bulk of this task.

key_results.claim: The circuit is organized into seven head categories.
key_results.quote: The circuit uses 7 categories of heads (see Figure 2) to implement the algorithm.

key_results.claim: The unmodified model performs strongly on pIOI and usually predicts the indirect object over the subject.
key_results.numbers: 100,000 dataset examples; mean logit difference 3.56; IO predicted over S 99.3% of the time; mean IO probability 49%
key_results.quote: Over 100,000 dataset examples, GPT-2 small has mean logit difference of 3.56 (IO predicted over S 99.3% of the time), and mean IO probability of 49%.

key_results.claim: All three Name Mover Heads copy name tokens much more reliably than an average head.
key_results.quote: All three Name Mover Heads have a copy score above 95%, compared to less than 20% for an average head.

key_results.claim: The proposed circuit is faithful to the full model, with a performance gap of 0.46 logit-difference units.
key_results.quote: For the circuit C from Figure 2, we find that |F (M ) − F (C)| = 0.46, or only 13% of F (M ) = 3.56.

key_results.claim: Greedy knockout searches found combinations for which the proposed circuit is substantially incomplete.
key_results.quote: However, the third resulted in sets K that had high incompleteness score: up to 3.09 (87% of the original logit difference).

key_results.claim: The circuit retains most of its task performance when the regular Name Mover Heads are knocked out, revealing compensatory backup heads.
key_results.quote: To our surprise, the circuit still worked (only 5% drop in logit difference).

key_results.claim: Adversarial passages that duplicate the indirect object cause the model to select the subject over the indirect object.
key_results.quote: We find that this significantly reduces the logit difference and causes the model to predict S over IO 23% of the time (Figure 8).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Some Duplicate Token and Induction Head validation checks were omitted because of time constraints.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: To fully validate the claimed function of the Duplicate Token and Induction Heads, we would want to perform additional checks that we omitted due to time constraints.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The implementation of the newly observed positional-signal function of Induction Heads was not investigated.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We did not investigate how this mechanism was implemented.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The origin and broader relevance of backup-head compensation remain unresolved.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: More work is needed to determine the origin of this phenomenon and if such compensation effects can be observed beyond our special case.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The authors do not understand the S-Inhibition Heads' attention patterns or the effects of MLPs and layer norms.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Those include the attention patterns of the S-Inhibition Heads, and the effect of MLPs and layer norms.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: GPT-2 small is far smaller than state-of-the-art language models, making scaling an unresolved challenge.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Second, the number of parameters in GPT-2 small is orders of magnitude away from state-of-the-art transformer language models.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The mechanisms operating on the adversarial duplicated-IO examples were not fully understood.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Moreover, we do not have a full understanding of the mechanisms at play in these adversarial examples.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The adversarial examples may be discoverable without using the circuit, limiting evidence for the circuit's unique downstream value.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Despite being inspired by our understanding of our circuit, those examples are simple enough that they could have been found without our circuit with enough effort.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Greedy completeness searches exposed large incompleteness scores that were not semantically interpretable.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: However, the third resulted in sets K that had high incompleteness score: up to 3.09 (87% of the original logit difference).

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The principal IOI distribution is synthetic and highly structured, so the circuit may reflect template-specific token and position regularities rather than general linguistic reasoning.
MLPs, layer norms, and embedding matrices were excluded from the main causal circuit, so the head-only account is not a full mechanistic explanation of the model's computation.
Completeness is assessed with random, classwise, and greedy searches rather than exhaustive subset enumeration, leaving unsearched knockout combinations unresolved.
Backup and negative heads make the apparent circuit intervention-dependent, so components discovered after ablation may reflect compensation rather than the model's normal computation.
The experiments do not establish robustness across natural-text distributions, longer contexts, substantially different syntax, or broad distribution shifts.
The paper provides no direct evidence about KV-shared architectures, per-layer embedding extraction, factual-recall circuits, or transfer to Gemma 4 E2B.
The CPU cost of repeated path-patching forward passes is not evaluated, limiting confidence that the complete protocol will transfer to the lab's hardware constraint.
data.relevance_to_lab: High methodological relevance: causal path patching, activation patching, backward tracing from logits, attention-pattern analysis, residual-stream/unembedding projections, and explicit induction-head tests closely match the lab's activation-patching, logit-lens, and induction-head tracing interests. The controlled IOI benchmark and knockout framework could provide a reproducible test case before adapting the workflow to Gemma 4 E2B layers 15–34 and per-layer embedding readouts. However, the paper does not address KV sharing, factual recall, per-layer embeddings, or CPU tractability, and its GPT-2 small circuit may not transfer directly to a different architecture and scale.
